title: Slide a hot air-fryer basket out from under its retaining hooks, lift it by the handle and set it on the heat-proof mat
instruction: The chips are done. Take the basket out of the air fryer and set it on the green mat; let go and keep both fingers at least 3 cm from the basket.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), z above the table top (z = 0.7475 m, smooth laminate, friction 0.5). Air fryer housing (fixed, graphite painted steel, 25 kg stand-in, friction 1.2): 22 x 28 x 26 cm at (57, 0), front face at x 46; a red lamp (2 x 2 cm on the front face, 3 x 3 cm on the top face) is lit. Drawer plate (fixed, grey steel, 25 kg, friction 1.2): 18 x 23 x 3.6 cm at (37, 0), x 28 to 46, against the housing; the drawer is shown pulled out to its stop and its side walls are omitted. Two hook assemblies (fixed, same plate): a post 2 x 1 x 7.6 cm at y +/-10.7 (x 43.7 to 45.7) and an overhang 2 x 1.6 x 0.8 cm at y +/-9.4 whose underside is at z 10.4 cm; each overhang reaches over a basket flange. Basket (loose, orange-painted steel, 450 g, friction 0.32, handle black): floor 17 x 17 cm, walls 0.5 cm thick and 6 cm tall, floor centre at (37.2, 0), floor underside on the plate (z 3.6 cm), so it spans x 28.7 to 45.7. Two rear flanges, each 3 x 0.9 x 0.5 cm (x 42.7 to 45.7, y +/-8.5 to +/-9.4, z 9.1 to 9.6), sit under the hook overhangs with 8 mm vertical and 8 mm lateral clearance. Handle: two posts 3.7 x 2 x 3 cm at y +/-4.5 standing off the front wall (x 25 to 28.7) and a bar 4 x 12 x 2 cm across their ends (x 21 to 25, z 7.6 to 9.6; bar centre at x 23, z 8.6); the basket with handle is 24.7 x 18.8 x 6 cm. The basket must be pulled at least 2.0 cm toward the robot for the flanges to clear the overhangs, 2.8 cm with margin. Heat-proof mat (fixed, green silicone, 25 kg stand-in, friction 1.2): 20 x 20 x 1.0 cm at (35, -22) (x 25 to 45, y -32 to -12). Both arms start open at their ready poses. The layout is the same in every trial. Real build: the housing and drawer plate are 3D-printed PLA blocks bolted to the table (this replaces the 25 kg fixed mass), the hooks are printed PLA with 8 mm clearances, the basket is a 17 x 17 x 6 cm sheet-steel or printed box with printed handle and flanges, and the mat is a 1 cm silicone or foam pad bolted to the table. Material as modelled: every object is a rigid body with only the size, mass and friction stated here; nothing deforms and nothing heats.
scoring: Final state plus faults. ON MAT: the basket's floor centre within 10 mm of the mat's centre, its floor underside within 3 mm of the mat's top (z 1.0 cm), tilt at most 3 degrees, turned at most 10 degrees. RELEASED: both gripper centres at least 3 cm from every part of the basket and both grippers at least 90% open. STILL: the basket moves slower than 1 cm/s at the end (1 s hold). UNHOOKED: the basket's floor centre has been at least 2.0 cm toward the robot of its start, so both flanges are clear of the hook overhangs, and it has been lifted at least 2 cm in that state. Permanent zero, even if recovered: at any time a gripper's pad bottom comes within 12 mm of an orange wall, the basket floor, a flange, the housing, the drawer plate or a hook (hot surfaces; only the black handle may be touched). 1.0: ON MAT, no fault, RELEASED, STILL. 0.75: ON MAT, no fault, but RELEASED or STILL fails. 0.5: UNHOOKED and lifted, no fault, but the basket ends elsewhere than on the mat. 0.25: the basket was slid at least 2.8 cm toward the robot at some time, no fault. Else 0. Doing nothing scores 0; a held or hovering basket does not count as on the mat. Possible scores: 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Real trial: tape (2.8 cm slide, 1 cm centring), a photo of the end state, and a video for hot-surface contact.
fidelity: No heat is simulated: hot parts are marked by the lit lamp and orange paint and enforced by contact scoring on the gripper geometry. The basket (17 x 17 x 6 cm, 450 g) is at the small end of real baskets (compact units); the drawer's side walls are omitted so the arm can pass, and the handle stands 6.2 cm proud so the 94 mm gripper fits. The hooks are real keyed geometry with 8 mm clearances, not a script. Housing and drawer plate are fixed 25 kg parts.
context: Taking a hot basket out of an air fryer is an everyday job for home cooks and for Cooks, Short Order (O*NET 35-2015.00) and Food Preparation Workers (35-2021.00). The housing and basket are at frying temperature (red lamp lit), so only the black handle may be touched, and the basket goes on a heat-proof mat. The one ability: a keyed release (slide the basket 3 cm toward you until its flanges leave two retaining hooks, then lift) done through the handle. Source: the Instant Vortex Mini manual warns to use only the basket handle to lift and carry the basket, https://manuals.plus/m/85ecea6fda5793fb8ff3f918a9e3e8ba5f4450226e875ad8002a9312ad1377c3. Why a robot task: hook geometry fixes the direction and a hot-surface no-touch zone constrains every motion. Closest on the board: TK-PSHKS8 (hot pot down), TK-RSPMXH (two-latch lid); new here: hooks decide the removal direction.
reset_notes: Push the basket fully back against the housing with its flanges under the hooks (floor centre at x 37.2 cm, y 0); put the mat at (35, -22); both grippers open and clear at ready. The first frame shows the red lamp lit and the basket in the drawer.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms stayed near their bases and never touched the basket); demo: 1.0 (right arm slid the basket 3.1 cm toward the robot out of the hooks, lifted it by the handle, set it on the green mat, let go and withdrew)
